sources.title: N8n 2.30.4 – Safely restore a missing node with original ID and version protection
sources.text: We need guidance on safely repairing an existing workflow in self-hosted n8n 2.30.4 , without risking unintended changes.
taskExcerpts: We need guidance on safely repairing an existing workflow in self-hosted n8n 2.30.4 , without risking unintended changes.

spans.text: We need guidance on safely repairing an existing workflow in self-hosted n8n 2.30.4 , without risking unintended changes. Current situation The workflow is inactive and unpublished. It currently contains 26 nodes. One Data Table node ( n8n-nodes-base.dataTable , typeVersion 1.1) is missing. The original missing node has the ID b4-17 . We have verified backups of the current workflow and the original 27-node design. Only the missing node and its two connections should be restored. All existing nodes, credentials, webhook paths, workflow settings, and the workflow identity must remain unchanged. A previous attempt to paste a partial JSON fragment into the editor unexpectedly changed the workflow title. We stopped and subsequently restored the intended title. We do not want to repeat this approach without reliable safeguards.
Does n8n 2.30.4 reliably protect against concurrent modifications when saving a workflow through the editor?
For the API endpoint PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id} , does versionId provide effective optimistic locking in this specific version?
What is the recommended approach for restoring exactly one missing node and its two connections in an existing inactive workflow?
